searches.query: The warehouse received my ordinary return. What is the longest published sequence until the bank-card credit appears, assuming normal approval?

chunks.text: When refunds arrive  The returns team normally inspects an ordinary parcel within five business days after warehouse receipt. Once the return is approved, the store submits the refund within two business days. A bank-card provider may then take another three to five business days to show the credit. These stages happen in sequence. A carrier delivery notification is not the same event as a completed inspection.  For planning, the longest published path is five business days for inspection, two for submission, and five for the card provider: up to 12 business days after warehouse receipt. That is a policy estimate, not a live payment-status lookup. Weekends and published holidays do not count as business days. A missing component or a dispute over condition can require further review.  Gift recipients receiving store credit are sent that credit after approval. The three-to-five-day bank-card processing period does not apply to issuing store credit. This page does not identify whether a particular return has been received, approved, or refunded.

Payment authorization holds  When an order is placed, the card provider may show a pending authorization. The store captures payment when the order is dispatched. A pending entry and a captured payment are different states; the pending line alone does not prove a completed charge. If an order is cancelled before capture, the store releases the authorization rather than issuing a refund for a captured payment.  The card provider typically removes a released authorization within three to seven business days. The exact display time depends on that provider. Support cannot turn this policy range into a promise that a particular bank will remove the hold tomorrow. If a customer reports both a pending entry and a completed entry, check the payment record before calling it a duplicate charge.  The order-change policy controls whether an order can still be cancelled. This article does not extend the 30-minute request window or reverse warehouse processing. It also does not contain actual transaction records, card details, or authorization identifiers.

This page does not identify whether a particular return has been received, approved, or refunded. For that, support needs the live return record. A screenshot of the original purchase receipt does not show the refund's current status.
A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process. The seven-day transport-report window does not shorten a separately applicable manufacturing warranty.

A return request is not itself a refund. Customers receive a receipt after the inspection is complete. Original outbound delivery charges are not refunded for a change of mind. The return-label policy explains who pays for sending an item back. Do not send an item to the warehouse without an approved return request.

The 14-day mismatch report window is a separate route from the manufacturing warranty. Do not describe it as a 14-day change-of-mind return right. Stock for a replacement outlet product is not guaranteed.

Exchanging a size or color  For a domestic order, an eligible unused product can be exchanged for a different size or color of the same model. The exchange keeps the original paid item price even if the current listing price changed. The replacement must be available when the request is approved. Exchanges into a different model are handled as a return followed by a new purchase at the new model's price.  The warehouse holds an approved replacement for seven calendar days. The customer must hand the returning parcel to the carrier within that period. The hold does not last until the parcel physically arrives at the warehouse. If the dispatch deadline passes, the reservation is released and availability must be checked again. Support cannot promise stock from a catalog description.  Exchanges use the same unused-condition and eligibility-window rules as standard returns. The store does not offer direct international exchanges. An international customer may use the return route if eligible and place a separate new order.

Returning a gift  A recipient with a gift receipt can return eligible unused gear within 45 calendar days after delivery. The recipient receives store credit equal to the item's paid price. The recipient does not receive a refund to their own bank card. If the purchaser requests the return through their original order, the normal purchaser-refund rules apply instead.  A gift receipt hides the price on the paper presented to the recipient, but the order system still records the actual amount paid. Discounts are included in that amount. For a product bought as part of a discounted bundle, use the bundle-allocation policy to calculate the paid amount for that product. Do not substitute the current shelf price, the pre-discount price, or the price of a replacement item.  Gift returns still require an approved request and must meet the condition requirements. The gift window does not make a used jacket returnable. The return-label fee follows the ordinary return-label policy.

Reporting delivery damage or the wrong product  Report visible transport damage or a wrong product within seven calendar days after delivery. Keep the outer packaging and photograph the label, packing materials, and affected item. The support team compares those details with the shipment record before approving the claim. If the item is unsafe to use, stop using it while the report is assessed.  An approved wrong-product or delivery-damage return receives a prepaid label. The customer does not pay the ordinary USD 7 change-of-mind label fee for that approved return. The team confirms whether a replacement or another remedy will be provided. A report being opened does not prove replacement inventory exists or establish a delivery date for the replacement.  Damage involving a rechargeable battery follows the separate damaged-battery procedure. Do not put a leaking or swollen battery in an ordinary return parcel even when support is investigating delivery damage. A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process.

answer.answer: The longest published sequence for a bank-card credit after warehouse receipt is up to 12 business days. This comprises: 5 business days for inspection, 2 business days for the store to submit the refund, and 5 business days for the card provider to show the credit. These stages happen in sequence.
